## Motivation

First code PR of RFC #43949 (part 2 of 4): the monokernel plugin, which runs most of a decoder layer, including its TP all-reduce, as one or two persistent launches. No model is registered here, so `--enable-monokernel` refuses to start; the DeepSeek-V4.1 spec comes in the next PR.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes: no spec is registered and the switch is off by default. CPU unit tests under `test/registered/mono` (40 pass).

+"""Monokernels: persistent kernels that run most of a decoder layer, including its TP all-reduce, in one or two
+launches (RFC #43949).
+
+SGLang calls the plugin's hooks, each a no-op while ``--enable-monokernel`` is off: ``handle_monokernel`` in the
+config pipeline (``guards``: refuse an unsupported setup with every reason), then ``load_tensor`` / ``loaded``,
+``attach``, ``route`` and ``kernel`` in each process (``runtime``). ``spec`` holds what a model declares and the
+registry of specs. Shared device primitives live in ``common_<vendor>/``, each model's kernels, spec and glue in
+``<model>_<vendor>/``.
+
+A failed wait stops its launch and flags every peer, whose waits stop too (``common_hip/guard.py``): a rank finishes a
+step only with every peer's data for it, so no token of a failed step is sent and SGLang stops the process tree.
+"""
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.guards import handle_monokernel
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.runtime import attach, kernel, load_tensor, loaded, route
+
+__all__ = ["attach", "handle_monokernel", "kernel", "load_tensor", "loaded", "route"]

+"""Check mode (``SGLANG_TEST_MONO_CHECK=1``, debugging only): the first ``SGLANG_TEST_MONO_CHECK_STEPS`` (default 4) eager
+mono steps also run every routed layer's module path on copies of its inputs, and log each output's max |diff|
+against it. Graph captures (and so replays) are never checked: run with --disable-cuda-graph. The module path's
+cache writes land before the kernel's, which rewrites them; a step that checked is not meant to be served from.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import Mapping
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+# the SGLang names this module reads (pinned by test_mono_contract)
+SGLANG_READS = ("sglang.srt.environ.envs",)
+
+
+def requested() -> bool:
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+    return envs.SGLANG_TEST_MONO_CHECK.get()
+
+
+class Checker:
+    def __init__(self, rank: int) -> None:
+        self.rank = rank
+        from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+        self.limit = envs.SGLANG_TEST_MONO_CHECK_STEPS.get()
+        self.steps = 0
+        self._logged = False
+
+    def begin_step(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether this step's routed layers are checked (uniform over ranks: same env, same capture state)."""
+        if self._logged:
+            self.steps += 1
+            self._logged = False
+        return self.steps < self.limit and not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+
+    def compare(
+        self,
+        layer_id: int,
+        rows: int,
+        pairs: Mapping[str, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
+    ) -> dict[str, float]:
+        """``pairs``: name -> (kernel output, module output). Synchronizes."""
+        diffs = {}
+        parts = []
+        for name, (out, ref) in pairs.items():
+            out_f, ref_f = out.float(), ref.float()
+            diffs[name] = (out_f - ref_f).abs().max().item()
+            parts.append(
+                f"{name} max|diff| {diffs[name]:.4g} (ref max {ref_f.abs().max().item():.4g})"
+            )
+        logger.info(
+            "[mono-check][rank %d] step %d layer %d (%d rows): %s",
+            self.rank,
+            self.steps,
+            layer_id,
+            rows,
+            ", ".join(parts),
+        )
+        self._logged = True
+        return diffs

+# HIP monokernel common (shared device and plan code)
+
+What every monokernel family on HIP shares: `device/` (traced inside kernels: tagged mailbox, bounded waits
+(`device/guard.py`), wave / math / packing primitives, MX helpers, timeline stamps), `plan/` (plain Python: execution
+model, region layout, build keys, arithmetic on ints and traced values alike, the hand-off trace), `guard.py` (the
+wait deadline, the guard words, fault injection) and `peer.py` (symmetric peer memory). It imports no model and
+holds no model constant. ATOM's other host mechanisms (step fence, compile-only builds, kernel ABI tables, timeline
+reader) and `device/select.py` / `plan/check.py` were dropped: the DeepSeek-V4.1 path never used them.
+
+## Origin
+
+Vendored from [ROCm/ATOM](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM) @ 454d0e3023, `atom/mono/{device,plan}` (MIT, header kept
+in every file).
+
+## Local changes
+
+- `device/sync.py` `Mailbox`: `tag=` for kernels that tag hand-offs with a step epoch instead of `layer + 1` (nothing
+  cleared between steps); a raw address (no `Addr`) is accepted as device-scope scratch and reported by the hand-off
+  check as unnamed (`plan.trace.note_unnamed`).
+- `device/ops.py` `ld_i32`: optional cache policy `cm` (default 0 = the previous load).
+- `plan/arith.py`: `imin`, `imax`, `i32`, and a `cdiv` that works on traced values; `plan/shard.py` uses it.
+- `plan/build_key.py` `source_digest`: paths relative to this `gfx950` package (a family passes its own directory and
+  `"common"`).
+
+## Families using it
+
+- `deepseek_v41/`: every device helper (its private copy of this code was removed; see its SOURCE.md).
+- MiniMax-M3 (not ported yet): of the 30 helpers in zijiecode/sglang-mono-amd `kernels/ops/mono/common_hip.py`,
+  22 are identical to `device/`, 1 differs only in its docstring (`unlikely`), 5 differ (`kernel_symbol`, `xshfl`,
+  `block_max`, `bf2_f32`, `Mailbox`) and 2 are M3-only (`release_stores`, `ar_pack_sumsq`).
+
+## Not used by any family yet
+
+`device/{ranks,select}` beyond `peer_bases` / `sum_partials`, `plan/check`, parts of `plan/trace`, and helpers such as
+`fp8x8_bf16_pk` (which the M3 kernels use). Kept until the MiniMax-M3 port decides what it needs.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# Copyright (C) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+"""Fail-stop inside the kernel (RFC #43949 section 7), the device half. A wait that misses its deadline, or sees
+that another rank stopped, records why, flags every rank, fences, and stops its launch with a store to address 0
+(a GPU fault): a launch never runs on after a failed wait. A satisfied wait costs nothing extra -- the clock and the
+stop flag are read only once the first poll comes back stale. Word layout: ``common_hip.guard``."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+from flydsl._mlir import ir
+from flydsl._mlir.dialects import llvm
+from flydsl.expr import range_constexpr, rocdl
+from flydsl.expr.typing import T, as_ir_value
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.common_hip.device.ops import (
+    CM_SYS,
+    ld_i32,
+    load_ptr64,
+    memrealtime,
+    traced,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.common_hip.guard import (
+    ERROR,
+    REASON_DEADLINE,
+    REASON_PEER,
+    SITE,
+    STOP,
+    ZERO,
+    site_id,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Guard:
+    """A launch's view of the guard words: ``own`` (this rank's, traced address), ``peers`` (every rank's,
+    this one included), ``ticks`` (the deadline, traced Int64). ``fault_site`` / ``fault_tag``: a build's
+    injected stall (tests): the waits on that region stay pending from that hand-off tag on."""
+
+    own: object
+    peers: tuple
+    ticks: object
+    fault_site: str = ""
+    fault_tag: int = 0
+
+
+def guard_from_args(
+    own, table, tp: int, ticks, fault_site: str = "", fault_after: int = 0
+):
+    """``table``: the i64 addresses of every rank's guard words. A launch pair ``e`` tags its hand-offs 2 e + 1
+    (K1) and 2 e + 2 (K2), so pair ``fault_after`` on is tag 2 * fault_after + 1 on."""
+    peers = tuple(load_ptr64(table, p) for p in range_constexpr(tp))
+    return Guard(own, peers, fx.Int64(ticks), fault_site, 2 * fault_after + 1)
+
+
+def _word_ptr(addr):
+    return fx.inttoptr(fx.PointerType.get(T.i32, fx.AddressSpace.Global, 4), addr)
+
+
+@traced
+def _stop(g: Guard, site: int, reason):
+    fx.llvm.atomic_or(_word_ptr(g.own + 4 * ERROR), fx.Int32(reason))
+    fx.llvm.atomic_cas(_word_ptr(g.own + 4 * SITE), fx.Int32(0), fx.Int32(site))
+    for p in range_constexpr(len(g.peers)):
+        fx.llvm.atomic_xchg(_word_ptr(g.peers[p] + 4 * STOP), fx.Int32(1))
+    fx.llvm.memory_fence()
+    rocdl.s_waitcnt(vmcnt=0)
+    # the ZERO word is 0 at run time, so the store goes to address 0 and faults; read, it cannot be folded away
+    null = fx.Int64(ld_i32(g.own, ZERO, cm=CM_SYS))
+    ptr = llvm.IntToPtrOp(ir.Type.parse("!llvm.ptr<1>"), as_ir_value(null))
+    llvm.StoreOp(as_ir_value(fx.Int32(reason)), ptr.result, alignment=4, volatile_=True)
+
+
+def stall_of(g, region: str, tag):
+    """The injected stall of a wait on ``region`` at hand-off ``tag`` (traced bool), or None."""
+    if g is None or not g.fault_site or g.fault_site != region:
+        return None
+    return fx.Int32(tag) >= fx.Int32(g.fault_tag)
+
+
+@traced
+def guarded_spin(load_all, pending, g: Guard, region: str, stall=None):
+    """``load_all()`` until ``pending`` clears, within ``g``'s deadline; a stop otherwise (see the module doc)."""
+
+    def busy(v):
+        return pending(v) if stall is None else (pending(v) | stall)
+
+    v = load_all()
+    t0 = fx.Int64(0)
+    stop = fx.Int32(0)
+    while busy(v) & (stop == 0):
+        rocdl.s_sleep(1)
+        v = load_all()
+        now = memrealtime()
+        t0 = (t0 == 0).select(now, t0)
+        peer = ld_i32(g.own, STOP, cm=CM_SYS) != 0
+        late = (now - t0 > g.ticks).select(fx.Int32(REASON_DEADLINE), fx.Int32(0))
+        stop = peer.select(fx.Int32(REASON_PEER), late)
+    if stop != 0:
+        _stop(g, site_id(region), stop)
+    return v

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# Vendored from ROCm/ATOM @ 454d0e3023: atom/mono/device/mx.py
+# Copyright (C) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+"""FP8 / MX arithmetic the mono kernels share: the E4M3 range, E8M0 scale
+codes, the byte of a scale in aiter's ``shuffle_scale`` layout, an FP4 weight
+tile's operand loads and the scaled MFMA that takes them.
+
+An E8M0 code is a biased exponent; ``pow2(code)`` is the scale it stands for.
+"""
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
+from flydsl.expr import rocdl
+from flydsl.expr.typing import T
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.common_hip.device.ops import CM_NT
+
+FP8_MAX = 448.0
+# the f8f6f4 MFMA's operand formats (cbsz / blgp)
+FP8, FP4 = 0, 4
+UNIT_SCALE = 127  # the E8M0 code of 1.0
+
+
+def clamp_fp8(v):
+    """``v`` clamped to the E4M3 range."""
+    return fx.max(fx.min(v, fx.Float32(FP8_MAX)), fx.Float32(-FP8_MAX))
+
+
+def code_ceil(v):
+    """Biased exponent of the smallest power of two >= ``v`` (v >= 0, finite),
+    clamped to [1, 254]: the codes a scale may take."""
+    bits = v.bitcast(fx.Int32)
+    e = ((bits >> 23) & 0xFF) + ((bits & 0x7FFFFF) != 0).select(
+        fx.Int32(1), fx.Int32(0)
+    )
+    return fx.max(fx.min(e, fx.Int32(254)), fx.Int32(1))
+
+
+def pow2(code):
+    """The fp32 power of two a biased exponent stands for."""
+    return (code << 23).bitcast(fx.Float32)
+
+
+def rcp_pow2(code):
+    """1 / ``pow2(code)``, exact (code in [1, 253]): x times it is x / scale
+    bit for bit, a multiply where the division is a dozen instructions."""
+    return ((254 - code) << 23).bitcast(fx.Float32)
+
+
+def scale_index(row, col, cols):
+    """Byte of e8m0 scale (row, col) in aiter's ``shuffle_scale`` layout:
+    ``view(rows/32, 2, 16, cols/8, 2, 4).permute(0, 3, 5, 2, 4, 1)``."""
+    r32, a, b = row // 32, (row // 16) % 2, row % 16
+    c8, d, e = col // 8, (col // 4) % 2, col % 4
+    return ((((r32 * (cols // 8) + c8) * 4 + e) * 16 + b) * 2 + d) * 2 + a
+
+
+def fp4_tile_load(r_w, base, rg, k, st, at):
+    """A lane's 16 B of an FP4 weight's (16, 16)-shuffled 16-row group ``rg``

+    Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL: lambda c: (_read(c, "pp_size") or 1) > 1,
+    Feature.MULTI_NODE_TP: lambda c: (_read(c, "nnodes") or 1) > 1,
+    Feature.DP_ATTENTION: lambda c: bool(_read(c, "enable_dp_attention")),
+    Feature.EXPERT_PARALLEL: lambda c: (_read(c, "ep_size") or 1) > 1,

+    Feature.SPEC_VERIFY: lambda c: _read(c, "speculative_algorithm") is not None,
+    Feature.UNEVEN_VERIFY: _verify_uneven,
+    Feature.TWO_BATCH_OVERLAP: lambda c: bool(_read(c, "enable_two_batch_overlap")),
+    Feature.LORA: lambda c: bool(_read(c, "enable_lora")),

+    size, ISA."""

+    reasons = feature_refusals(cfg, spec) + requirement_refusals(cfg, spec)

+    if reasons:

+def handle_monokernel(server_args) -> None:
+    """The config hook: refuse at startup (every reason at once) when the model has no spec or the resolved

+    from sglang.srt.arg_groups.model_override_base import model_config_of

+"""The monokernel runtime (RFC #43949 sections 2 and 5): the calls SGLang makes in each process, with the switch off
+each a no-op.
+
+  load_weights(), each tensor         tensor = load_tensor(model, name, tensor); loaded(model) at the end
+  precompile_kernels_after_loading()  attach(loop_module, architecture)
+  the layer loop                      plan = route(loop_module, forward_batch) once a forward;
+                                      span = kernel(plan, i, "layer_in") at each span start (None: the normal layer)
+
+A step not routed to the kernels runs the model's layers exactly as before; the module tree, parameter names and weight
+loading are untouched by the switch. Routing is a function of what every rank sees alike (forward mode, row count,
+batch size), so under CUDA graphs the decision baked in at capture is what every replay repeats.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import logging
+import time
+from collections import Counter
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Callable, NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono import check, guards
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mono.spec import (
+    Feature,
+    LayerKernel,
+    MonoContext,
+    MonoModel,
+    MonoSpec,
+    MonoStep,
+    Point,
+    Span,
+    check_spans,
+    load_spec,
+    span_label,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# the SGLang names this module reads (pinned by test_mono_contract)
+SGLANG_READS = (
+    "sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_config.Backend",
+    "sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_exec",
+    "sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_parallel",
+    "sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_server_args",
+)
+
+_RUNTIME = "_mono_runtime"  # attribute of the layer-loop module that holds its runtime
+
+
+class MonoUnsupported(Exception):
+    """The loaded model or runtime configuration is outside what the kernels serve."""
+
+
+def tp_agree(ok: bool, group) -> bool:
+    """True when every rank of ``group`` (a CPU / gloo group, or None for one rank) passed ``ok`` true. A kernel waits
+    in-kernel on every peer, so a rank that turned monokernels off alone, or failed to build what the others launch,
+    must take every other rank with it; every rank calls this at the same point."""
+    if group is None:
+        return ok
+    flag = torch.tensor([int(ok)], dtype=torch.int32)
+    dist.all_reduce(flag, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN, group=group)
+    return bool(flag.item())
+
+
+def _server_args():
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_server_args
+
+    return get_server_args()

+@functools.cache
+def _spec(architecture: str) -> Optional[MonoSpec]:
+    return load_spec(architecture)
+
+
+# ---- routing ----
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Decision:
+    step: Optional[MonoStep]  # None: the model's own path
+    reason: str  # why not, for metrics ("" when routed)
+
+
+def decide(
+    spec: MonoSpec,
+    ctx: MonoContext,
+    *,
+    is_decode: bool,
+    is_verify: bool,
+    rows: int,
+    batch_size: int,
+) -> Decision:
+    if not (is_decode or is_verify):
+        return Decision(None, "not decode")
+    if is_verify and Feature.SPEC_VERIFY not in spec.features:
+        return Decision(None, "verify unsupported")
+    if rows not in ctx.limits.widths:
+        return Decision(None, "width")
+    if batch_size < 1 or rows % batch_size:
+        return Decision(None, "rows not a multiple of the batch")
+    step = MonoStep(
+        rows=rows,
+        batch_size=batch_size,
+        is_verify=is_verify,
+        query_len=rows // batch_size,
+    )
+    why = spec.eligible(ctx, step)
+    if why:
+        return Decision(None, why)
+    return Decision(step, "")
+
+
+def decide_for_batch(spec: MonoSpec, ctx: MonoContext, forward_batch) -> Decision:
+    mode = forward_batch.forward_mode
+    rows = (
+        int(forward_batch.input_ids.shape[0])
+        if forward_batch.input_ids is not None
+        else 0
+    )
+    return decide(
+        spec,
+        ctx,
+        is_decode=mode.is_decode(),
+        is_verify=mode.is_target_verify(),
+        rows=rows,
+        batch_size=int(forward_batch.batch_size),
+    )
+
+
+# ---- the runtime a model holds ----
+
+
+class Route(NamedTuple):
+    spans: tuple[Span, ...]
+    kernel: LayerKernel
+    step: MonoStep
+    cache: dict  # per-step memo the spec's glue may fill once and share across the step's layers
+    checker: Optional[check.Checker] = (
+        None  # set on the steps check mode compares against the module path
+    )
+
+
+class MonoRuntime:
+    def __init__(self, spec: MonoSpec, ctx: MonoContext, model: MonoModel) -> None:
+        self.spec, self.ctx, self.model = spec, ctx, model
+        self.spans = dict(model.spans)
+        check_spans(self.spans)
+        self._kernels: dict[int, LayerKernel] = {}
+        self.decision = Decision(None, "no step yet")
+        self.step_cache: dict = {}
+        self.counts: Counter = Counter()
+        self.state = dict(spec.state_bindings(ctx, model))
+        self.checker = check.Checker(ctx.tp_rank) if check.requested() else None
+        self._checking = False
+        logger.info(
+            "mono kernels on: spec=%s widths=%s layers=%d (%s)",
+            spec.name,
+            list(ctx.limits.widths),
+            len(self.spans),
+            dict(Counter(span_label(s) for s in self.spans.values())),
+        )
+
+    def begin_step(self, forward_batch) -> Decision:
+        self.step_cache = {}
+        d = decide_for_batch(self.spec, self.ctx, forward_batch)
+        if d.step is not None and d.step.rows not in self._kernels:
+            d = Decision(None, "width not built")
+        self.decision = d
+        self._checking = (
+            d.step is not None
+            and self.checker is not None
+            and self.checker.begin_step()
+        )
+        self.counts["mono" if d.step is not None else f"fallback:{d.reason}"] += 1
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing() and self.ctx.tp_rank == 0:
+            # replays never reach Python: the capture is where a graph's path is decided
+            logger.info(
+                "mono graph capture: %d rows -> %s",
+                int(forward_batch.input_ids.shape[0]),
+                "mono" if d.step is not None else f"model path ({d.reason})",
+            )
+        return d
+
+    def routed(self, layer_id: int) -> Optional[Route]:
+        """The route when this step runs layer ``layer_id`` on the kernels, else None."""
+        step = self.decision.step
+        if step is None:
+            return None
+        spans = self.spans.get(layer_id)
+        if spans is None:
+            return None
+        binding = self.state.get(layer_id)
+        if binding is not None:
+            binding.wait_ready()
+        return Route(
+            spans,
+            self._kernels[step.rows],
+            step,
+            self.step_cache,
+            self.checker if self._checking else None,
+        )
+
+    def build_widths(self, widths) -> dict[int, int]:
+        """Build every width now, collectively (bytes of scratch each allocated); any rank failing refuses mono."""
+        scratch = {}
+        for rows in widths:
+            before = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() if torch.cuda.is_available() else 0
+            kernel = None
+            try:
+                kernel = self.model.kernel(rows)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "mono %s: building the %d-row kernels failed", self.spec.name, rows
+                )
+            if not tp_agree(kernel is not None, self.ctx.cpu_group):
+                guards.raise_if_refused(
+                    "model",
+                    self.spec.name,
+                    [f"building the {rows}-row kernels failed on a TP rank"],
+                )
+            self._kernels[rows] = kernel
+            if torch.cuda.is_available():
+                scratch[rows] = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before

+
+def attach_spec(
+    model,
+    spec: MonoSpec,
+    *,
+    server_args,
+    hf_config,
+    tp_rank: int,
+    tp_size: int,
+    cpu_group,
+    device,
+) -> MonoRuntime:
+    """The runtime of ``spec`` on ``model``, its widths not built yet."""
+    guards.raise_if_refused("model", spec.name, list(spec.model_disable_reasons(model)))
+    isa = guards.current_isa()
+    limits = guards.device_limits(spec, isa)
+    if limits is None:
+        guards.raise_if_refused(

+        server_args=server_args,
+        hf_config=hf_config,
+        tp_size=tp_size,

+# ---- weight loading ----
+

+"""CPU test of the monokernel plugin's contract with SGLang (RFC #43949 section 10): every module under
+kernels/ops/mono declares the SGLang names it imports in ``SGLANG_READS``, and every declared name still exists. An
+SGLang refactor that breaks the plugin fails here and names the file to repair."""
+
+import ast
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import sglang
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+ROOT = Path(sglang.__file__).parent
+PLUGIN = ROOT / "kernels/ops/mono"
+
+
+def srt_imports(tree: ast.Module) -> set[str]:
+    names = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and (n.module or "").startswith("sglang.srt"):
+            names |= {f"{n.module}.{a.name}" for a in n.names}
+        elif isinstance(n, ast.Import):
+            names |= {a.name for a in n.names if a.name.startswith("sglang.srt")}
+    return names
+
+
+def declared(tree: ast.Module) -> set[str]:
+    for n in tree.body:
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and any(
+            isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "SGLANG_READS" for t in n.targets
+        ):
+            return set(ast.literal_eval(n.value))
+    return set()
+
+
+def module_source(module: str):
+    rel = Path(*module.split(".")[1:])
+    for p in (ROOT / rel.with_suffix(".py"), ROOT / rel / "__init__.py"):
+        if p.is_file():
+            return p
+    return None
+
+
+def top_level_names(path: Path) -> set[str]:
+    out = set()
+    for n in ast.parse(path.read_text()).body:
+        if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
+            out.add(n.name)
+        elif isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
+            out |= {t.id for t in n.targets if isinstance(t, ast.Name)}
+        elif isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name):
+            out.add(n.target.id)
+        elif isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):
+            out |= {(a.asname or a.name).split(".")[0] for a in n.names}
+    return out
+
+
+class TestSglangReads(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_every_srt_import_is_declared(self):
+        for path in sorted(PLUGIN.rglob("*.py")):
+            tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+            used, decl = srt_imports(tree), declared(tree)
+            rel = path.relative_to(ROOT)
+            self.assertEqual(used - decl, set(), f"{rel}: add these to SGLANG_READS")
+            self.assertEqual(
+                decl - used,
+                set(),
+                f"{rel}: SGLANG_READS lists names it no longer imports",
+            )
+
+    def test_every_declared_name_exists(self):
+        for path in sorted(PLUGIN.rglob("*.py")):
+            for name in sorted(declared(ast.parse(path.read_text()))):
+                module, _, attr = name.rpartition(".")
+                src = module_source(module)
+                self.assertIsNotNone(src, f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: {module} is gone")
+                self.assertIn(
+                    attr,
+                    top_level_names(src),
+                    f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: {name} is gone; repair this module",
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
